writeup: TIC 294860388 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.0826 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 1.24 percent, yielding a strong detection signal with a signal-to-noise ratio of 88.2. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis shows a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 6.6, though the centroid offset of 2.9 arcsec from the target raises an important question: TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate this star from a nearby bright neighbor, with the dimming centroid located only 0.007 pixels closer to the target than to the competitor - within the instrument's known systematic uncertainty of 0.10 to 0.3 pixels.
